impact: After a serve killed by SIGKILL or OOM, another OS user binding 127.0.0.1:<port> receives the Authorization Bearer shell token on the first attempt and on every retry. Reproduced with a scratch squatting Bun.serve and a dead pid in endpoint.json.
suggested_fix: Serve the remote surface on a Unix domain socket in the 0700 remote dir, or use a challenge-response. At minimum refuse in target() when process.kill(pid, 0) fails and mint a fresh shell token on every serve start.

problem: Telegram update_id was used as a monotonic dedupe key. The hub persisted a highWater and dropped update_id <= highWater, the poller asked for offset highWater + 1, the shell dropped id <= lastCompleted but still acked it, and serve dropped updateId <= completed[session].
impact: The Bot API chooses a random update_id after a week without updates. A bot nobody uses for a week is a normal case, and a new id below the persisted mark is either treated by Telegram as confirmed or skipped by the hub or the shell, so every message is lost and nothing reports it.

problem: The poller-lock takeover is racy. A serve that has created poller.lock but not yet written its pid looks pid-less to a second serve, which unlinks it and creates its own; two serves that both see a dead holder can unlink each other's fresh file.
impact: Two hubs run on the same sessions.json and queues (lost updates, double sends) and one gets a 409 and stops for good. ensureShellToken had the same empty-read window and could tell the second serve to delete the token file under the first.
suggested_fix: Write the pid to a temp file and link() it to the lock name, take a stale lock over by renaming it aside and re-checking, and treat a young empty lock as held.
evidence: Read src/remote/poll-lock.ts and createOwnerOnlyFileExclusive in src/lib/config-dir.ts at 34bf0f80: open with wx precedes the write of the pid.

verification.evidence: at 4f1326d2: poll-lock.ts createWhole() writes the pid to a private staging file and link()s it to poller.lock, so the lock never exists empty; a stale lock is renamed aside, inspected, and put back if what was moved is a live holder's fresh lock; a pid-less lock younger than EMPTY_LOCK_GRACE_MS (5 s) is treated as held. poll-lock.test.ts passes (10 tests), including 'the lock is never visible half-written', 'a young lock with no pid in it is somebody mid-write: held, not taken over' and 'two takers of the same dead lock: the one that loses the race puts the winner's lock back and refuses'. ensureShellToken is gone: shell-token.ts mintShellToken writes through writeOwnerOnlyFileAtomic (temp file plus rename) and is called only after the lock is held, so a second serve neither reads an empty token file nor rotates it.

disposition.evidence: src/remote/poll-lock.ts createWhole() writes a staging file and link()s it (never empty), stale lock renamed aside and re-checked, young pid-less lock held (EMPTY_LOCK_GRACE_MS); ensureShellToken replaced by mintShellToken (atomic, only after the lock is held). Tests: src/remote/poll-lock.test.ts.
